New: a closed notch that tells you more at a glance, more detail on every session, an option to keep the Mac awake with the lid closed while agents work, and a different sound for each kind of event.

What's new

- The closed notch: one dot per session, coloured by state (working, waiting on you, failed, done), a small pet that reacts to what the agents are doing, a prod dot, and a bar for the weekly limit. When something needs you the wing shows a short word for it instead of a bare icon. The pet and dots move gently; Reduce Motion, a locked screen and sleep stop the motion. Setup → Effects has switches for the pet and for "Calm until needed".
- Context use per session: each Claude Code row shows how full the context window is, turning amber and then red as it nears the point where it compacts, with one notification before it does. The row says "compacting" while that runs.
- Failed turns: a turn that ends on an API error (rate limit, overloaded, sign-in, billing, server error, output limit) marks the session failed with the reason, a red dot on the closed notch and a notification.
- Git and CI on the row: the branch, the number of uncommitted files and unpushed commits, and a mark for the latest Bitbucket pipeline or EAS build on that branch. A click on the mark opens the run.
- Stay awake, lid closed (Setup, and the Machine panel; off unless turned on): keeps the Mac running with the lid shut, only while an agent is working and for about two minutes after. It lets go when the battery falls under 20%, when the Mac runs hot, when you turn it off or quit, and by itself within 90 seconds if the app is killed. It needs the helper: Setup shows "Helper update needed" with an Update… button if yours is older. A closed laptop sheds heat poorly, so do not run it in a bag.
- Sounds: nine soft sounds, one each for an agent needing you, a finished turn, a failed turn, context nearly full, a production alert, a failed build, a passed build, pull request news, and a dropped VPN or critical memory. Setup → Sounds has a master switch, a volume, and a switch and a play button per event. Sounds: Material Design sound resources by Google, CC BY 4.0 (levels adjusted).
- Watchdog stories from Datadog can notify (a switch in Setup, on unless turned off).
- The header shows at most two chips, with the rest behind a menu. Pull requests live in one panel, and the open notch shows the few that need you beside the sessions.

Fixes

- A click on the Prod chip with one Watchdog story opened a "not found" page. It now opens the story, or the monitors list when the story has no page.
- Session rows no longer swap places while agents work. Rows that need you sit on top, the one that asked first stays first, and every other row keeps its place.
- Compact rows: the Idle chip no longer touches the Details button, and the Details button no longer covers a subagent card.
- Memory: reading a large transcript at launch could take several hundred megabytes for a moment; it is now read in small pieces. The Setup window is released when closed.
- Less work while closed: the closed notch no longer redraws every second, and a hook event reaches the list in about 20 ms instead of about 300 ms.
- Text sizes follow one scale, links are checked before they open, and controls have VoiceOver labels.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

After upgrading, open Setup once and click Set Up so the three new Claude Code hook events are added.

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later.
